[P3] 学校
从小灰狼家到松塔学校，只有一条路。
那么问题就来了。
这个夏天，大红帽和她的奶奶搬到了这里。大红帽不仅是个大个子，而且还不友好。她和小灰狼都走森林里的这条小路去上学。

[P4] 在大红帽搬来之前，小灰狼很喜欢去上学。他喜欢听他的爪子走在路上发出的啪嗒啪嗒声；也喜欢微风轻轻拂过他的胡须，吹得树叶沙沙作响。

当然，他最最喜欢他的黄色午餐篮子，里面装满了他最爱吃的食物。

[P5] 大红帽最喜欢的事，就是
捉弄、嘲笑和吓唬小灰狼了。
有时，她突然从树
后面跳出来。
有时，她突然伸出她的
大脚把小灰狼绊倒。
有时，她
偷偷跟在小灰狼
身后，拽他的尾巴。
小灰狼试着不抱怨。
他试着不哭。
他试着不和大红帽说话。

[P6] “明确告诉她，不准欺负你。”妈妈告诉他。
“让她知道，你不喜欢她捉弄你。”
但一点儿也不管用。小灰狼问爸爸妈妈，他该怎么办。

[P7] “住手！”当大红帽不停地向小灰狼扔橡子的时候，小灰狼说，“我不喜欢这样！”
大红帽大笑起来。
“但是我喜欢。”大红帽说。
接着她捡起了一个大橡子，一下子砸中了小灰狼的鼻子。

[P8] “挺起腰板站直，这样你看起来会很强大。”爸爸告诉他。

[P9] 于是，大红帽又一次拽他尾巴的时候，小灰狼尽可能地挺起腰板站直。
但是，大红帽大笑着说：‘我才不怕你这个小灰狼呢。’她得意地哈哈大笑。

[P10] 小灰狼不知道该怎么办。一天早晨，一个黑影突然挡住了路。小灰狼抬头一看，原来是大红帽。
“你要去哪里？”大红帽问。

小灰狼想跑，但是大红帽挡住了他的去路，说：“别溜得那么快。”
大红帽一把从小灰狼手里抢过来午餐篮子，边跑边喊：
“小花篮，小花篮，我有一个新篮子啦。”

[P11] 小灰狼伤心极了。他中午吃什么呢？
如果他没有把午餐篮子拿回家，爸爸妈妈
会怎么说他呢？他们会让那个红褐色的包
来装午餐吗？

[P12] 鹿老师陪他去找辅导员——无所不知的猫头鹰老师。
小灰狼把大红帽欺负他的事说了出来。
小灰狼到了学校，鹿老师问他怎么了。小灰狼
不敢告诉她，因为大红帽正盯着他呢。
辅导员

[P13] “听起来确实是个难题。”无所不知的猫头鹰老师说，“你试过解决这个问题吗？”
“我要求大红帽不要欺负我，就像我妈妈说的那样。”小灰狼告诉辅导员。“我在他面前挺起腰板站直，就像我爸爸告诉我的那样。”小灰狼说，“但是大红帽还是嘲笑我。现在她把我的午餐篮子都抢走了，我不知道该怎么办！”他边说边用尾巴擦眼泪。

[P14] “看上去你应该做一些大红帽不希望你做的事，”无所不知的猫头鹰老师说，“就像这样！”猫头鹰老师的头不停地转着。
小灰狼笑了。
“看，你笑起来多好看，”猫头鹰老师说，“我以前从来没注意到，你应该经常笑笑。”
小灰狼决定他以后要经常微笑。

[P15] 在回家的路上，当大红帽从树后跳出来的时候，小灰狼没有再哀求，也没有哭，他只是微笑着。
“你是在冲我笑吗？”大红帽问，“这是怎么了？”
小灰狼只是一直微笑着。其实，他很紧张地趴在那里不敢动。
“有什么好笑的？”大红帽问，向后退了一步说，“不许那样看着我！你想干什么，咬我吗？”
小灰狼笑了，这活多傻啊。小孩子才咬人呢。
“把这个丑篮子还给你，”大红帽说，“我才不要它呢！”
她把篮子扔到了地上。

[P16] 小灰狼高兴地笑出声来。无所不知的猫头鹰老师是对的。做一些大红帽不希望你做的事很有用。也许他早应该对她微笑了。他有一种感觉，大红帽以前没有得到过多少微笑。他确信她现在得到了。

小灰狼一路小跑回家。他的耳朵竖了起来，尾巴翘得高高的。他感觉比以前更强大，也更好啦。

[P3] School
From Little Gray Wolf's home to Pinecone School, there is only one path.
Then the problem arises.
This summer, Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother moved here. Little Red Riding Hood is not only tall, but also unfriendly. She and Little Gray Wolf both walk this forest path to school.

[P4] Before Little Red moved in, Little Gray Wolf loved going to school. He loved hearing the pitter-patter of his paws on the path; he also loved the gentle breeze brushing his whiskers and making the leaves rustle.

Of course, he loved his yellow lunch basket most of all, filled with his favorite foods.

[P5] The Little Red Riding Hood's favorite thing to do was
to tease, laugh at, and scare the little gray wolf.
Sometimes, she would suddenly jump out from behind a tree.
Sometimes, she would suddenly extend her big foot and trip the little gray wolf.
Sometimes, she
would sneak behind the little gray wolf
and pull his tail.
The little gray wolf tried not to complain.
He tried not to cry.
He tried not to talk to Little Red Riding Hood.

[P6] "Clearly tell her, don't bully you," Mom told him.
"Let her know you don't like her teasing you."
But it didn't work at all. The little gray wolf asked his dad and mom, what should he do?

[P7] "Stop it!" When Little Red Riding Hood kept throwing acorns at Little Gray Wolf, Little Gray Wolf said, "I don't like this!"
Little Red Riding Hood burst out laughing.
"But I like it," said Little Red Riding Hood.
Then she picked up a big acorn and threw it, hitting Little Gray Wolf right on the nose.

[P8] "Stand up straight with your back straight, then you'll look very strong," Dad told him.

[P9] Then, when Little Red Riding Hood pulled his tail again, the little gray wolf tried his best to stand up straight.
But Little Red Riding Hood laughed loudly: 'I'm not afraid of you, little gray wolf.' She laughed with delight.

[P10] The little gray wolf didn't know what to do. One morning, a dark shadow suddenly blocked the path. The little gray wolf looked up and saw it was Little Red Riding Hood.
"Where are you going?" asked Little Red Riding Hood.

The little gray wolf wanted to run, but Little Red Riding Hood blocked his way, saying, "Don't run so fast!"
Little Red Riding Hood snatched the lunch basket from the little gray wolf's hand and ran off, shouting:
"Little flower basket, little flower basket, I have a new basket!"

[P11] The little gray wolf was heartbroken. What would he eat for lunch?
If he didn't bring his lunch basket home, what would his parents say?
Would they make him use that reddish-brown bag for his lunch?

[P12] The deer teacher took him to see the counselor—the all-knowing owl teacher.
Little Gray Wolf told the counselor about how Little Red Cap had been bullying him.
Little Gray Wolf arrived at school, and the deer teacher asked him what was wrong. Little Gray Wolf
was afraid to tell her, because Little Red Cap was staring at him.
Counselor

[P13] "It does sound like a tough problem," said the all-knowing owl teacher. "Have you tried to solve it?"
"I asked Red Riding Hood not to bully me, just like my mom said," Little Gray Wolf told the counselor. "I stood up straight and held my head high in front of her, just like my dad told me to," Little Gray Wolf said. "But Red Riding Hood still laughed at me. Now she's taken my lunch basket, and I don't know what to do!" He said, wiping his tears with his tail.

[P14] "It looks like you should do some things that Little Red Hood doesn't want you to do," said the all-knowing owl teacher, "like this!" The owl teacher's head kept spinning.
Little Gray Wolf smiled.
"Look, you look so nice when you smile," said the owl teacher, "I never noticed before. You should smile often."
Little Gray Wolf decided he would smile often from now on.

[P15] On the way home, when Little Red Riding Hood jumped out from behind the tree, the little gray wolf didn't beg anymore, nor did he cry. He just smiled.
"Are you laughing at me?" asked Little Red Riding Hood. "What's wrong?"
The little gray wolf just kept smiling. In fact, he was trembling and crouched there, too scared to move.
"What's so funny?" asked Little Red Riding Hood, stepping back. "Don't look at me like that! What do you want? Are you going to bite me?"
The little gray wolf smiled. "That's so silly. Only children bite people."
"Give this ugly basket back to you," said Little Red Riding Hood, "I don't want it!"
She threw the basket to the ground.

[P16] The little gray wolf laughed out loud with joy. The all-knowing owl teacher was right. Doing things that Little Red Riding Hood didn't want you to do was very useful. Maybe he should have smiled at her long ago. He had a feeling that Little Red Riding Hood had never received many smiles before. He was sure she was getting them now.

The little gray wolf ran home happily. His ears stood up, and his tail curled high. He felt stronger and better than ever before.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《大红帽和小灰狼》的封面，展示了书名、副标题、作者、译者、出版社及美国心理学会官方授权标识，画面中一个女孩坐在树上，一只小动物背着书包在树下行走，背景为秋日森林。
[P2] 本页为绘本《大红帽和小灰狼》的扉页，展示了书名、副标题、作者、译者、出版社等信息，以及一个装满秋叶的红色提篮插图。
[P3] 本页描绘了森林小径上一只背着书包的小灰狼正走向学校，路标指向学校。文字说明从小灰狼家到松塔学校只有一条路，而大红帽和奶奶搬来后，她和小灰狼将共用这条上学路，由此引出潜在的冲突。
[P4] 本页描绘了小灰狼在大红帽搬来之前上学路上的愉快情景，他享受走路的声音和微风，也最喜欢他的黄色午餐篮子。
[P5] 本页描绘了大红帽在上学路上捉弄小灰狼的种种行为，如从树后跳出来、用脚绊倒他、偷偷拽他尾巴，而小灰狼则努力忍耐，试图不抱怨、不哭、不和她说话。
[P6] 小灰狼在洗澡时向父母倾诉，尽管妈妈建议他明确表达不满，但对大红帽的捉弄毫无作用，他不知如何是好。
[P7] 大红帽在树上向小灰狼扔橡子，小灰狼表示不喜欢，但大红帽却觉得有趣并继续扔，最终用一个大橡子砸中了小灰狼的鼻子。
[P8] 小灰狼在餐桌上吃饭，爸爸一边做煎饼一边告诉他要挺起腰板站直，这样看起来会很强大。
[P9] 大红帽再次捉弄小灰狼，拽他的尾巴，小灰狼努力挺直身体，但大红帽毫不在意，反而得意地大笑。
[P10] 大红帽在上学路上突然挡住小灰狼的去路，抢走了他的午餐篮子，并得意地跑开，小灰狼只能无助地站在原地。
[P11] 小灰狼因午餐篮子被大红帽抢走而伤心，担心自己中午吃什么，以及父母会如何责备他。
[P12] 小灰狼在学校向鹿老师求助，但因大红帽在场而不敢开口，最终在鹿老师的陪同下向辅导员猫头鹰老师倾诉了被大红帽欺负的事情。
[P13] 小灰狼向猫头鹰老师倾诉自己被大红帽欺负的经历，包括要求她停止欺负、挺直身体应对，但都无效，午餐篮子也被抢走，他感到无助并哭泣。
[P14] 猫头鹰老师建议小灰狼做些大红帽不喜欢的事，并鼓励他微笑，小灰狼听从建议，决定以后经常微笑。
[P15] 在回家的路上，大红帽突然出现，小灰狼没有哭闹，只是微笑。大红帽质问并嫌弃小灰狼的微笑，最终将他的午餐篮子扔在地上。
[P16] 小灰狼在被大红帽欺负后，听从猫头鹰老师的建议，选择微笑面对，感到内心强大并开心地跑回家。
[P17] 画面中小灰狼坐在草地上，面前散落着午餐篮子和食物，他低头看着篮子，神情平静，似乎在整理或检查被大红帽扔掉的午餐。
